title: Establish a suspension sag baseline
summary: Measure fork and rear-shock sag methodically and compare the result with the actual component or frame manufacturer’s recommended setup range.

tools.name: Manufacturer setup guide
tools.note: Use the exact fork, shock and frame guidance where available.

tools.name: Assistant
tools.note: Helpful for holding the bike while the rider assumes a normal position.

steps.title: Record the current setup first
steps.instruction: Before adjusting anything, record current pressure and external damping settings, and identify the manufacturer’s recommended starting procedure for the exact fork, shock and frame.
steps.why: A written baseline lets you return to the previous setup and avoids losing track of multiple simultaneous changes.
steps.warning: Do not copy another rider’s pressure or damping settings as if they were universal.
steps.check: Current settings are recorded and the correct setup guidance is available.

steps.title: Set a manufacturer-guided starting pressure
steps.instruction: Use a compatible shock pump and the manufacturer’s setup method to establish a starting air pressure for the rider and component.
steps.why: Air pressure sets the spring support that largely determines how far the suspension settles under load.
steps.warning: Stay within the component’s published pressure limits and follow its equalization/setup instructions.
steps.check: Starting pressure is set according to the correct component guidance.

steps.title: Settle into a repeatable riding position
steps.instruction: Cycle the suspension as directed by the manufacturer, then carefully assume the specified neutral or riding position without bouncing. Use an assistant if needed for balance.
steps.why: Sag measurement is useful only when rider position and suspension preparation are consistent.
steps.warning: Perform this on level, stable ground where you can safely support the bicycle.
steps.check: The rider position is stable and repeatable.

steps.title: Measure how far the suspension settled
steps.instruction: Use the component’s travel indicator or O-ring where appropriate, then measure the displacement using the manufacturer’s recommended method.
steps.why: Sag is a measured displacement, not a feeling. Consistent measurement gives a useful baseline for later adjustments.
steps.check: Sag has been measured using the correct reference points.

steps.title: Compare with the recommended range
steps.instruction: Compare the measured sag with the exact bike/component guidance. If adjustment is needed, change pressure in small deliberate increments and repeat the same measurement process.
steps.why: The purpose is a repeatable baseline within the intended setup range, not chasing a universal percentage.
steps.warning: Do not exceed published pressure limits. If correct sag cannot be achieved within the allowed setup range, stop and investigate the component/setup.
steps.check: Measured sag is documented and evaluated against the correct manufacturer guidance.
